newsitem.title: USA: Crown Cork sells unit for $105 million.
newsitem.headline: Crown Cork sells unit for $105 million.

text.p: Crown Cork & Seal Co. Inc. said Wednesday it sold its Crown-Simplimatic packaging machinery business to an investor group, including management, for $105 million.
The selling price includes $90 million in cash and $15 million in preferred stock that is convertible into about 20 percent of the common stock of Crown-Simplimatic, the company said.
The investor group included Key Equity Capital Corp., a Cleveland, Ohio, investment firm.
Proceeds from the sale will be used to pay off debt, Crown Cork said.
Crown-Simplimatic was formed last year by combining Crown Cork & Seal's machinery division with the Simplimatic Engineering business of Crown's CarnaudMetalbox subsidiary, the company said.
The combination created one of a handful of companies providing systems to fill and package beer bottles, the company said.
In 1996, Crown-Simplimatic generated 2 percent of Crown Cork & Seal's sales of $8.3 billion.
Crown Cork & Seal will have one representative on the seven-member board of directors, the company said.
